title: The Evening Brief: Simmons admits proxy betting; Kroenke enters MLB; Fernandez deal done
dek: Tuesday evening brought admissions of rule-breaking in legal sportsbooks, a landmark ownership transition in baseball, and the completion of the English transfer window. The day showed how sports betting's expansion into mainstream platforms is creating enforcement questions, while institutional upheaval continued in college athletics and professional soccer.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Bill Simmons's public admission of proxy betting on a regulated sportsbook revealed how easily account-access protocols can be breached, even at platforms operating under state oversight; the Massachusetts Gaming Commission is now reviewing whether enforcement suffices. Separately, Kroenke's agreement to acquire the Angels marks his entry into baseball, pending Q1 2027 closing.
bottom_line: Bill Simmons's proxy betting admission has reached the Massachusetts Gaming Commission for review; the outcome will determine whether FanDuel's account actions satisfied regulators or whether individual consequences follow. Kroenke's Angels acquisition is definitive but pending Q1 2027 closing, making that date the checkpoint for whether institutional conditions resolve and the deal advances to completion. Manchester City's Fernandez deal must clear his medical. UCLA's institutional spending, having consumed millions in buyouts, will test whether new leadership can stabilize the department's financial footing.
body: Tuesday evening added three major institutional shifts to a day already marked by tournament progress and roster moves. Bill Simmons admitted on his podcast that he allowed his daughter's boyfriend to log into his FanDuel account in Massachusetts and place bets on his behalf, a practice explicitly prohibited under state gaming law and the platform's terms of service. FanDuel has voided the bets and sanctioned the account; the Massachusetts Gaming Commission is now reviewing the case. The admission exposed how easily two-factor authentication protocols can be breached when the account holder shares credentials voluntarily, and it raises questions about whether operator reporting and account sanctions satisfy regulatory requirements or whether individual users face personal consequences for facilitating proxy betting.

In baseball ownership, Kroenke Sports & Entertainment announced a definitive agreement to acquire a controlling interest in the Los Angeles Angels from the Moreno family, pending closing in Q1 2027. The transaction marks Kroenke's entry into Major League Baseball and ends Art Moreno's 20-year tenure, during which the Angels have missed the postseason for eleven consecutive years and will miss again in 2026.

In soccer, the Premier League and English Football League transfer window closed at 23:00 BST on Tuesday, September 1, locking in moves across four tiers of English football. Manchester City completed its acquisition of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea for 125 million pounds, matching the joint-British transfer record and making Fernandez the first player in history to transfer for more than 100 million pounds twice. Newcastle secured Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille for 51.4 million pounds; Aston Villa added Ibrahim Mbaye from Paris St-Germain for 47 million pounds and Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Southampton for 29 million pounds. Arsenal moved Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona for 8.6 million pounds and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg at the same fee. The Scottish Premiership and Women's Super League transfer deadlines remain open through September 3.

On the regulatory front, Netflix signed a multiyear agreement with EverPass Media to distribute its expanded NFL games package to commercial establishments including bars and restaurants. The deal extends Netflix's out-of-home footprint as streaming platforms compete for sports audiences; EverPass is itself being acquired by London-based DAZN, with closing expected after regulatory approvals and an eventual rebrand to DAZN for Business.

In baseball roster moves, the San Diego Padres called up catcher Ethan Salas, age 20 and the franchise's top prospect, to the major leagues on Tuesday. The promotion signals long-term succession planning at the position.

At UCLA, the university's third major leadership reset in one year became official when the school fired Athletic Director Martin Jarmond and paid him a 6.5 million dollar buyout, citing a significant financial deficit. Jarmond's departure arrives days before new football coach Bob Chesney's debut and follows the firing of former head coach DeShaun Foster earlier in the year. The cascade of expensive personnel changes, with total buyouts now exceeding 12 million dollars, raises structural questions about athletic department oversight and spending control.
